examples.question_text:
Find the general solution of each differential equation.
(a) $y'=15e^{-3x}+2$
(b) $y'=8\cos 4x+6\sin 3x$
(c) $y'=\dfrac{7}{x}$, where $x\ne0$.
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}y&=\int(15e^{-3x}+2)\,dx\\y&=-5e^{-3x}+2x+C\end{align*}$
(b)
$\begin{align*}y&=\int(8\cos 4x+6\sin 3x)\,dx\\y&=2\sin 4x-2\cos 3x+C\end{align*}$
(c)
$\begin{align*}y&=\int\frac{7}{x}\,dx\\y&=7\ln|x|+C\end{align*}$
Each part has its own arbitrary constant.

examples.question_text:
Find the general solution of each differential equation.
(a) $y'=\sqrt{2x+5}$, where $x>-\dfrac{5}{2}$.
(b) $y'=6x\cos(x^2)$.
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}y&=\int(2x+5)^{1/2}\,dx\\y&=\frac{(2x+5)^{3/2}}{(3/2)\times2}+C\\y&=\frac{1}{3}(2x+5)^{3/2}+C\end{align*}$
(b) Since $\dfrac{d}{dx}\sin(x^2)=2x\cos(x^2)$,
$\begin{align*}y&=\int6x\cos(x^2)\,dx\\y&=3\sin(x^2)+C\end{align*}$
Each part has its own arbitrary constant.

examples.question_text:
Find the general solution of each differential equation.
(a) $xy'=8$, where $x>0$.
(b) $\dfrac{y'}{x}=e^{x^2+2}$, where $x\ne0$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Make $y'$ the subject.
$\begin{align*}y'&=\frac{8}{x}\\y&=\int\frac{8}{x}\,dx\\y&=8\ln x+C\end{align*}$
(b)
$\begin{align*}y'&=xe^{x^2+2}\\y&=\int xe^{x^2+2}\,dx\\y&=\frac{1}{2}e^{x^2+2}+C\end{align*}$
The stated domain restrictions still apply. Each part has its own arbitrary constant.

Integrate to find the general solution.
$\begin{align*}y&=\int(9x^2-4)\,dx\\y&=3x^3-4x+C\end{align*}$
Substitute $x=2$ and $y=7$.
$\begin{align*}7&=3(2)^3-4(2)+C\\7&=16+C\\C&=-9\end{align*}$
The particular solution is $y=3x^3-4x-9$.

examples.question_text:
Given $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{10}{(5-x)(5+x)}$, $y(0)=3$ and $-5<x<5$:
(a) Show that $\dfrac{10}{(5-x)(5+x)}=\dfrac{1}{5-x}+\dfrac{1}{5+x}$.
(b) Hence solve the initial value problem.
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{1}{5-x}+\frac{1}{5+x}\\&=\frac{(5+x)+(5-x)}{(5-x)(5+x)}\\&=\frac{10}{(5-x)(5+x)}\end{align*}$
(b) Integrate using the decomposition.
$\begin{align*}y&=\int\left(\frac{1}{5-x}+\frac{1}{5+x}\right)\,dx\\y&=-\ln(5-x)+\ln(5+x)+C\\y&=\ln\frac{5+x}{5-x}+C\end{align*}$
Both logarithm arguments are positive on $-5<x<5$.
Using $y(0)=3$,
$\begin{align*}3&=\ln\frac{5}{5}+C\\C&=3\end{align*}$
The particular solution is $y=\ln\dfrac{5+x}{5-x}+3$, for $-5<x<5$.

examples.question_text:
A curve satisfies $y''=12x+6$.
Its tangent at $(1,4)$ has gradient $8$.
Find the general solution, then the equation of this curve.
examples.solution_text:
Integrate twice, introducing a separate constant at each stage.
$\begin{align*}y'&=\int(12x+6)\,dx\\y'&=6x^2+6x+A\\y&=\int(6x^2+6x+A)\,dx\\y&=2x^3+3x^2+Ax+B\end{align*}$
This is the general solution.
The tangent gradient gives $y'(1)=8$.
$\begin{align*}8&=6+6+A\\A&=-4\end{align*}$
The point $(1,4)$ gives $y(1)=4$.
$\begin{align*}4&=2+3-4+B\\B&=3\end{align*}$
The curve has equation $y=2x^3+3x^2-4x+3$.

examples.question_text:
A tank contains $18$ litres of water initially. Water flows into it at a rate of $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=10-2t$ litres per minute, for $0\le t\le5$.
Find $V$ in terms of $t$.
examples.solution_text:
Integrate the rate with respect to $t$.
$\begin{align*}V&=\int(10-2t)\,dt\\V&=10t-t^2+C\end{align*}$
The initial volume gives $V(0)=18$.
$\begin{align*}18&=0-0+C\\C&=18\end{align*}$
Therefore $V=10t-t^2+18$ litres, for $0\le t\le5$.

examples.derivation: Termwise integration gives y=3x^3-3x^2+2x+C. Differentiating gives 9x^2-6x+2, matching the supplied derivative.

(a) Integrating gives -5e^(-3x)+2x+C. (b) The inner coefficients give 2sin(4x)-2cos(3x)+C. (c) Integrating 7/x gives 7ln|x|+C on intervals excluding zero. Each derivative matches its question, and each part has an independent constant.

(a) Integrating (2x+5)^(1/2) gives (2x+5)^(3/2)/3+C; differentiation cancels the factor (3/2)×2. (b) Since the derivative of sin(x^2) is 2x cos(x^2), the integral is 3sin(x^2)+C. Both adaptations follow source Foundation Q1(e–f).

(a) Rearranging gives y'=8/x, hence y=8ln x+C for x>0. (b) Rearranging gives y'=xe^(x^2+2), hence y=e^(x^2+2)/2+C on the stated intervals excluding zero. Differentiating both results verifies the rearranged equations.
Integration gives y=3x^3-4x+C. At x=2, 7=24-8+C, so C=-9. The final function has derivative 9x^2-4 and value 7 at x=2.

Adding the supplied fractions gives numerator (5+x)+(5-x)=10. Integration gives -ln(5-x)+ln(5+x)+C. Both arguments are positive on -5<x<5. At x=0 the logarithmic difference is zero, so C=3. Differentiation gives 1/(5-x)+1/(5+x), verifying the DE. The bare opening expression correctly uses a phantom equals gutter.
